newsitem.title: KENYA: Uganda 96/97 coffee exports may reach 4.3 mln bags.
newsitem.headline: Uganda 96/97 coffee exports may reach 4.3 mln bags.

text.p: Uganda's coffee exports may reach 4.3 million 60-kg bags in 1996/97, despite an outbreak of disease and severe drought, a senior official said on Wednesday
Paul Mugambwa, president of the Uganda Coffee Trade Federation, told Reuters in Nairobi drought was a major challenge for coffee expansion plans but did not critically affect exports.
He said in an interview that Uganda's coffee industry saw exports rising to about five million bags by 2000.

In 1995/96, Uganda exported a record of about 4.2 million bags. But the state policy Uganda Coffee Development Authority (UCDA) said at the time it saw exports easing to between 3.6 and 3.8 million bags.
"It is possible that our exports will reach 4.3 million bags," Mugambwa said. "That forecast is not out of line."
Last month, UCDA officials said exports could be hit by coffee wilt disease and drought in eastern Uganda.

But Mugambwa said expansion of land under coffee and an extensive programme in the recent past of replacing old trees compensated for that. He added that the new clonal robusta variety with higher yields ensured a better crop.
"It is true that drought has severely affected some plantations, especially in eastern Uganda. But we must say certain areas like western Uganda are not affected at all.
"Then there are areas where the crop is affected only minimally, like the total outturn is 52-54 percent compared to the normal average 56 percent," Mugambwa added.
Mugambwa was speaking on the sidelines of a meeting of coffee industry leaders from Uganda, Kenya, Tanzania and Ethiopia under the umbrella of the Belgium-based APROMA.

In Kampala, UCDA on Wednesday forecast total exports in the first half of the year at 2,740,228 bags worth $206,235,384 compared with 2,308,527 bags worth $226,069,619 in the corresponding period in 1995/96.
UCDA put coffee exports in the first five months of 1996/97 at 2,339,162 60-kg bags valued at $173 million from 1,870,415 bags valued at $185.46 million in the same period last season.

UCDA projected March exports at 401,066 bags worth $32.62 million, with total expectations for the second 1996/97 quarter of 1,449,132 bags worth $110,999,996. This would compare with 1,513,025 bags worth $138,021,551 in the same period last season.
UCDA blamed the fall in the March volume on a scaling down of the coffee season in central and eastern Uganda -- where drought is pronounced.
It said a decline in international prices in the first quarter forced farmers to sell large quantities and depleted stocks at the farm level.
